messages:
monitoring-bot: SEV-1 ALERT — prod: KV cache runaway + TP NCCL stalls detected on tp-kv-cluster. P99 generation latency > 10s, streaming sessions interrupted. Alerts fired: kv_cache.capacity_ratio > 0.9 ; nccl.stall_count >= 4 across multiple hosts. :rotating_light:
oncall: grabbed the page, joining. I'm pausing any non-urgent deploys.
devon: noticed an unusual spike in long-context traffic at ~22:10 UTC, coincides with the 'continuous-batch' experiment we toggled for tp models five hours ago. cb-new-log shows many multi-key requests.
lee: digging into shard metrics: several shards show asymmetric key distribution — one shard has 12x average keys compared to peers. That saturation is causing queuing and then NCCL barrier timeouts. excerpt: 
```
shard-metrics: shard-3 keys=48k rps=1.2k kv_used=95%
shard-metrics: shard-7 keys=3.6k rps=110 kv_used=22%
nccl: rank 2 rendezvous timeout after 60s
```
maya: Support reports multiple customers with streaming disconnects and unhandled 5xxs; some retried automatically which aggravated load. I've flagged top impacted accounts for priority outreach.
ops-bot: Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) disable continuous-batch for TP-enabled models; 2) enable shard-level ingress throttling; 3) move noisy sessions to standby pool. Approving actions on request.
oncall: executing quick rollback: /feature-flag disable continuous_batch_tp --by=oncall --env=prod. Also scheduling per-shard throttle: /kv throttle set --max-requests=60 --scope=tp-kv-shard.
ops-bot: COMMAND ACK: feature flag disable queued. throttle command applied to shards 0..11.
infra-bot: additional quick fix: cordon overloaded hosts (tp-kv-03, tp-kv-12) to stop new allocations and restart shard-agent with KV_GC_AGGRESSIVE=1 on those nodes. This will push evictions and reduce memory pressure.
lee: applying GC restart on tp-kv-03 then tp-kv-12. restart logs: 
```
[tp-kv-03] shard-agent: stopping
[tp-kv-03] shard-agent: KV_GC_AGGRESSIVE=1 set
[tp-kv-03] shard-agent: started, eviction draining
```
devon: after rollback and cordons, eviction rate dropped within 2m, and NCCL stall count decreased. however P95 still ~2.2s above baseline for bursty requests.
monitoring-bot: STATUS UPDATE: kv_cache.capacity_ratio -> 0.6 (stable), nccl.stall_count -> 0 for 7m. Alert auto-resolved.
maya: customer impact summary for handoff: 6 customers saw streaming interruptions, median disruption 3m. CS notified and support tickets created.
oncall: handoff notes: disabled TP continuous-batching experiment, cordoned two hosts, enabled aggressive KV GC, applied per-shard throttle. Leaving core mitigations in place for 1 hour then gradual uncordon.
lee: root cause hypothesis: continuous-batching increased simultaneous multi-shard lookups and created skewed key hot-spots. That led to prolonged collective windows in NCCL; under skewed partitions an NCCL rendezvous bug surfaced causing stalls. Essentially a combination of workload shift + a latent rendezvous edge-case.
ops-bot: recommended post-incident actions: 1) revert continuous-batch config for TP until we add shard-aware batching; 2) add synthetic long-context canary traffic to rollout pipeline; 3) implement automatic shard hot-key detection and re-sharding trigger; 4) add fast-fail on NCCL rendezvous timeout to backoff batching instead of full stall.
infra-bot: collecting artifacts: nccl traces, dmesg, shard-agent logs uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/2210000000/artifacts/. Please include these in postmortem.
devon: owners assigned: Devon (runtime batch), Lee (tp infra/sharding), Maya (customer comms). oncall handing off to next_oncall — keep alerts unmuted until follow-ups are scheduled.
support-agent: scheduling customer update: will send interim note within 2 hours and notify engineering when PM is ready.
monitoring-bot: reminder scheduled: postmortem kickoff 2026-03-16 09:30 UTC.
oncall: closing live thread — incident mitigated. If any anomalies reappear, escalate immediately.
